text: Does the short exact sequence 0 → ℤ →×2 ℤ → ℤ/2ℤ → 0 split?
choices: No — a splitting would need an element of order 2 in ℤ, but ℤ is torsion-free
Yes — every short exact sequence of abelian groups splits
Yes — ℤ/2ℤ is a free ℤ-module
No — because the map ×2 is not injective
explanation: A right splitting s: ℤ/2ℤ → ℤ would send the generator to an element x with 2x = 0 and x ≠ 0 (else g∘s ≠ id) — impossible in ℤ. Equivalently ℤ ≇ ℤ ⊕ ℤ/2ℤ. This nonzero class generates Ext¹(ℤ/2ℤ, ℤ) ≅ ℤ/2ℤ.
